title: The Pannier-jar
year_evidence: 扉に『PUBLISHED BY THE AMERICAN FOLK-LORE SOCIETY … 1924』、序文の署名に『April, 1924.』
text:
Vassel Edwards, Retirement, Cock-pit country.

There was a man at slave time had a wife, and the wife kept two other
men. The husband of that wife was working out. One night, one came
first and then the house-master came home. And they had a big jar
called a pannier-jar, and the wife took the man and put him into the
pannier-jar. Afterward the other man came in, and when he saw the
house-master was frightened and he told the house-master he had come to
borrow the pannier-jar. The house-master told him he could take it, and
the woman helped him up with the pannier-jar. And when he got part of
the way, he said, “Poor me bwoy! if it wasn’t for this pannier-jar, I
would be dead tonight!” The other man in the pannier-jar said, “Brar,
same meself!” And he got frightened and heaved down the pannier-jar,
mashed it up and killed the man in there.
paragraphs: There was a man at slave time had a wife, and the wife kept two other men. The husband of that wife was working out. One night, one came first and then the house-master came home. And they had a big jar called a pannier-jar, and the wife took the man and put him into the pannier-jar. Afterward the other man came in, and when he saw the house-master was frightened and he told the house-master he had come to borrow the pannier-jar. The house-master told him he could take it, and the woman helped him up with the pannier-jar. And when he got part of the way, he said, “Poor me bwoy! if it wasn’t for this pannier-jar, I would be dead tonight!” The other man in the pannier-jar said, “Brar, same meself!” And he got frightened and heaved down the pannier-jar, mashed it up and killed the man in there.
語り手 ヴァッセル・エドワーズ(コックピット地方、リタイアメント)

奴隷の時代に、ある男に女房がいて、その女房はほかに男を二人囲っていた。女房の亭主は外へ働きに出ていた。ある晩、まず一人が来て、それから家の主人が帰ってきた。家には籠壺という大きな壺があって、女房は男をその籠壺に入れた。そのあとにもう一人の男が入ってきて、家の主人がいるのを見て怖くなり、籠壺を借りに来たのだと主人に言った。主人は持っていっていいと言い、女房は籠壺を担ぐのを手伝ってやった。男が道の半ばまで来たとき、こう言った。「おれもかわいそうな男だ! この籠壺がなかったら、今夜は死んでたろうよ!」 すると籠壺のなかの男が言った。「兄弟、おれも同じだ!」 男は怖くなって籠壺を投げ落とし、壺は割れて、なかの男は死んでしまった。
